title: INVERSE CONSTITUTIONAL AI: COMPRESSING PREFERENCES INTO PRINCIPLES

bias_targets.methodology: Using the Inverse Constitutional AI (ICAI) framework to generate and test principles on pairwise preference datasets, measuring the accuracy and relevance of rules that favor overly lengthy or redundant responses.
Applying ICAI to identify and quantify annotator preferences for specific structural formatting and tone, such as a preference for numbered lists or formal language.

Evaluating principles generated by ICAI to measure how often annotators disproportionately favor responses that present a definitive stance without nuance over more balanced, objective, or neutral answers.

Generating and comparing group-specific constitutions using the PRISM dataset to interpret and evaluate divergent AI model preferences among annotator subgroups born in different geographical regions.
